Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I pulled a short pack together and attached a one-page workflow + a preliminary answers doc. High level answers below; Monica (sec) and Aditya (product) are looped for technical detail and final artifacts.

Highlights:
- Workflow: Redwood supports three modes — Hosted (Redwood-managed TLS termination + HSM/soft-KMS inside our environment), Dedicated (customer-dedicated pools where we can terminate or pass through TLS), and Private (VPC/on-prem where all crypto can be customer-controlled). Diagram attached (redwood-hsm-byo-overview.pdf).
- BYOK import: we support PKCS#11-compatible HSMs (CloudHSM, Thales/Entrust PKCS#11 modules) and KMIP for HSM vendors that expose it. For cloud KMS we support import of key material where the cloud provider allows it (e.g., AWS KMS external key material patterns). For on-prem HSMs we support PKCS#11 and direct provisioning via our secure provisioning tool with attested channels.
- Key object types: HSM-backed objects can be provisioned as signing-only (non-exportable) or as encryption keys depending on customer policy. Non-exportability is enforced by the HSM policy and our runtime only uses PKCS#11/CloudHSM calls; we never export plain key material.
- Rotation: we support key versioning + envelope encryption. Recommended cadence is: signing keys — annual key rotation with interim ephemeral session keys as needed; DEKs (data encryption keys) — quarterly or per-major-release depending on workload. We do rolling re-wraps: new key material gets provisioned and active, and existing data is re-wrapped lazily/online to avoid downtime.
- TLS: Hosted API by default terminates TLS at our edge (Edge LB with FIPS-capable crypto). For Dedicated/Private we support TLS pass-through and customer-managed certs; Private supports customer-controlled mTLS within the VPC. Certificate rotation automation (ACME/automation hooks) is available for Dedicated and Private.

Attached: redwood-hsm-byo-overview.pdf and rfi-responses-cryptography-redwood-v1.docx (answers + checklist). Monica/Aditya — can you add HSM attestation artifacts and PKI guidance (esp. for Medivance's desire for vendor attestation)?

Also, available for a technical deep dive Wed/Thu — what time works for your SecurOps group?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — copying the security details you requested. Below are the operational facts and evidence we can provide immediately:

1) Supported import/provisioning methods
- PKCS#11: we support vendor PKCS#11 modules for HSMs used in customer on-prem or dedicated deployments. Key objects are instantiated inside the HSM and never leave plaintext scope.
- KMIP: supported for vendors who provide KMIP endpoints; we can act as a KMIP client for provisioning and lifecycle ops.
- CloudHSM: for AWS CloudHSM we use the standard PKCS#11 interface and can provision keys directly into the cluster; we also support CloudHSM-backed KMS constructs.
- Direct import: for BYOK imports where the vendor allows, we support secure import via encrypted key blobs and an attested import workflow (challenge/response + signed import log).

2) Attestation & evidence
- Available: FIPS 140-2/140-3 certificates from the HSM vendor (we can share vendor certs and FIPS validation references).
- HSM attestation: for certain vendors we can produce an HSM attestation package (serial, module identifiers, and a signed attestation stating key policies).
- Audit trails: all key lifecycle events (create/import/rotate/destroy) are logged and can be streamed to customer SIEM (Syslog/S3/Kinesis). We provide signed operation timestamps.

3) Signing-only vs. decrypt-capable keys
- You can request key templates that restrict usage to signing (no decrypt/unwrap). Enforcement is done by HSM ACLs + our runtime checks.

4) Rotation & re-wrap strategy
- We use envelope encryption: Master keys (HSM-protected) encrypt DEKs. Rotation process: provision new HSM key (KMS-level), start issuing new DEKs wrapped by new master, and perform lazy rewrap of persisted data. For high-sensitivity flows we offer scheduled background rewrap jobs to reach full migration within a defined window (configurable).

5) TLS specifics
- Cipher suites: we support modern TLS 1.2+ and TLS 1.3 cipher suites (AEAD, ECDHE). Edge termination uses FIPS-validated crypto modules where customers have a compliance requirement.
- mTLS: supported within Private and Dedicated deployments; can be enforced at the ingress and service mesh layers.
- Cert rotation: we offer automation hooks (ACME for public certs) and integration points for customer KMSs to store cert private keys.

Evidence artifacts we can supply this week: HSM vendor FIPS certs, a sample PKCS#11 import logfile (redacted), and a signed attestation PDF. I attached the attestation PDF we can share now (attestation-thales-fips-cert-2026.pdf).

If you have specific vendor constraints (Entrust, Thales, Yubico HSM), tell us which and we'll tailor the artifact set.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
